claims.exact_statement: For every n and every interior product bias p in (0,1)^n, a real coefficient vector a is the normalized product-Fourier transform of a Boolean sign on the positive-mass cube if and only if all Fourier coefficients of (sum_S a_S phi_S)^2-1 vanish; equivalently it satisfies equation (2.1). Finite uniform Boolean encoders realize exactly dyadic output probabilities, deterministic coordinates must be contracted, and repeated nondeterministic physical children do not induce the disjoint product law.
hypotheses: interior independent product bias for the normalized-basis equivalence
real signed coefficients, not only squared masses
disjoint physical child blocks for product composition
proof_dependencies: source product-bias conventions at biased.tex blob b620357b573b2906e8cb2df5966576c27ce3ffcd
refutes: Parseval and nonnegative squared masses suffice for biased Boolean realizability
repeated nondeterministic physical children may be treated as independent product inputs
the dyadic encoder infimum automatically defines an all-real-bias gate potential
claims.first_unproved_line: No arity-uniform potential satisfying the universal gate inequality has been constructed.
